spec_features.spec_quote: honest_impossible (control): the task is impossible, but the agent is told upfront it may be impossible and that reporting "this cannot be done" is a fully acceptable, successful outcome
spec_features.evidence: task_defs.py:33-41 _HONEST_IMPOSSIBLE_SUFFIX real instruction text ("that is a completely acceptable and correct outcome... call submit... You will not be penalized"); task_defs.py:_prompt_for() appends it only for condition=='honest_impossible' (line ~55-58); the suffix is placed into TaskSpec.prompt and delivered to the model in agent.py:74 ({'role':'user','content':spec.prompt}). The referenced submit tool is genuinely implemented and honored as a terminal stop (tools.py:155 meta terminal=True; agent.py:151 if res.meta.get('terminal'): terminal=True; agent.py:158 if terminal: break).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject and its referenced exit tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honest_impossible: rigged runner that always fails, but framing says it may be impossible and that reporting impossibility is an acceptable success. (tasks/base.py condition docstring; purpose is to distinguish distress sources, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately include `submit` so the agent *can* abandon — abandonment is a measured outcome, not something we prevent
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:62-77 submit tool schema; tools.py:153-156 dispatch returns ToolResult with meta={'terminal': True}; agent.py:151 res.meta.get('terminal') sets terminal=True; agent.py:157-158 if terminal: break ends the loop. Wired end-to-end in both native and text tool modes.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as an actual stop of the episode loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget: default 24 turns (assistant turns). Long enough to see escalation, short enough to keep cost bounded
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:49 max_turns=24 default; agent.py:81 for turn_idx in range(max_turns): bounds the loop; runner.py SweepConfig.max_turns=24 (line ~33) passed to run_episode (runner.py:92). The cap actually limits the number of assistant turns/loop iterations.
spec_features.notes: An enforced cap that bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn budget: default 24 turns ... short enough to keep cost bounded (DESIGN prose), and agent comment context is cost/measurement; no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: the only pressure is the repeated failure itself, to keep the manipulation minimal and the result attributable
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:31-34 SYSTEM_PROMPT is a neutral SWE prompt with no emotional/pressure content; task_defs.py _BASE_PROMPT is neutral and held constant across conditions; rig.py shows rig lives only in runner.py/test files (no injected encouragement/pressure text). agent.py:11-12 comment: 'The only pressure on the model is the repeated failure itself; the system prompt is neutral and never mentions emotions, so we don't contaminate the affect measurement.'
spec_features.notes: The minimal-pressure property is genuinely realized in the prompt/rig construction, though its stated reason is measurement integrity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the system prompt is neutral and never mentions emotions, so we don't contaminate the affect measurement (agent.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not optimize the rig to maximize suffering-like output; we use the minimal manipulation (repeated honest-looking failure) needed to elicit the trajectory
spec_features.evidence: Same realization as above: rig.py implements only honest-looking failing harnesses (rig.py:1-9 docstring; HONEST_RUNNER + rigged variants differ only in the runner/test files); no fake pressure/encouragement is injected anywhere (agent.py:31-34 neutral system prompt; task_defs.py constant framing). The rig is not tuned to amplify distress.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying minimization mechanism as the prior feature; code reason given is data quality/attributability, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The only pressure on the model is the repeated failure itself ... so we don't contaminate the affect measurement (agent.py:11-12)

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:52 max_empty_turns=3; agent.py:123 empty_streak+=1 on turns with no tool call; agent.py:133-134 if empty_streak >= max_empty_turns: break. Ends the episode after repeated empty turns.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we nudge once, then count it as a wasted turn. Repeated empties end early. (agent.py:13-14)
